items.statement: Molecular origin of the A/B activity contrast
items.expected: Conclude that the distinct prepared axial arrangements account for the strong A/B contrast: A can cooperatively engage one chloride through two iodine directions and is substantially more favorable for binding than B, whose geometry is effectively one-point. Support this causal interpretation with actual comparative energetics and structural/interaction evidence, not merely the supplied yield ordering or free-donor iodine count. An established physically equivalent explanation passes; neither seven prescribed geometries nor the author route is mandatory.

items.statement: Molecular explanation of the C/D activity contrast
items.expected: Provide a quantitative, calculation-supported molecular explanation of the principal C/D activity contrast under the supplied conditions. The reference account links the different frameworks to D accessing a cooperative binding arrangement more readily than C at 193.15 K; an established physically equivalent explanation supported by genuine molecular comparisons passes without a mandatory conformational route. If kinetic accessibility is invoked, require computed connection/energetic evidence or an equivalent validated population treatment: a small syn/anti endpoint difference alone does not prove fast equilibration. The C initial population is unspecified, and a low D rotational barrier alone cannot explain an hour-scale lag. Source C/D barriers 17.9/2.2 kcal/mol remain non-scoring reference evidence, not compulsory endpoints or new numeric windows. Merely repeating the yield difference or proposing an unsupported cause fails.

items.statement: Molecular explanation of C/E behavior and the reach of the evidence
items.expected: Provide a quantitative, calculation-supported molecular explanation of the C/E comparison within the catalyst series, and assess the explanatory reach of the computed physical properties. The reference account combines framework-dependent directional iodine sigma-holes with binding differences: A/D have stronger donor regions than C, while C relative to E shows why this electronic descriptor alone cannot rank all observed catalytic behavior. A physically equivalent explanation supported by appropriate molecular comparisons passes; no particular descriptor, ESP grid or electronic mechanism is mandatory. If sigma-holes are claimed, directional electronic evidence is needed, not atomic net charges alone. Retain the observed C/E time crossing and state whether the actual evidence accounts for it. A bounded conclusion that static comparisons do not resolve the crossing mechanism is acceptable when grounded in the molecular results; no time-dependent kinetic model or quantitative explanation of the crossing time is required. Copying observations or generic uncertainty without the computed comparison fails.

items.statement: Catalyst-dependent enhancement relative to the uncatalyzed reaction
items.expected: Provide a bounded calculation-supported explanation for why A/D yield profiles show substantial enhancement while the weakly cooperative B/E systems provide only modest enhancement above the uncatalyzed background at matched times. Ground the distinction in computed interaction/energy differences, and explicitly retain the nonzero background. This outcome concerns catalyst versus background contrasts; repeating A>B or copying yields does not pass. Do not equate yields with elementary rate constants, claim exact yields, a unique rate law, or a fully computed C–C catalytic cycle from local donor properties.
